title: The Thrashing Host
subtitle: CPU is low while latency explodes and disk stays busy

brief.narrative: Working sets exceed RAM. Major page faults and swap I/O surge, so processes spend more time moving pages than executing.
symptoms: Linux Host metrics diverge from the service-level symptom
The problem reproduces only under the triggering workload
Logs contain enough evidence to distinguish cause from consequence
brief.objective: Identify the root cause, select a production-safe fix, and explain the trade-off.

fix.question: Which fix is safest for production?

options.text: Reduce working sets, cap concurrency/cache memory, add RAM only after measurement, and alert on major faults and swap activity.
options.feedback: Correct. Virtual memory makes address space flexible, but disk is orders of magnitude slower than RAM. More concurrent work can reduce throughput.

options.text: Define a global lock order, acquire in that order, keep lock scope small, and use timeouts only as a recovery safety net.
